newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end higher, palladium surges.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end higher, palladium surges.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended higher across the board on Monday, led by a surge in palladium futures, following higher spot prices and the dollar's firmer tendency against the yen, traders said.

The spot July palladium contract, which has no daily price limit, expired at noon, up 56 yen at 809 yen, with 10 lots of deliveries. October, December and February palladium rose by their 24 yen per gram daily limits at the close.
"For PGM futures, traders were quick to buy on any price dips. Lingering uncertainty over Russian supplies made it hard for market players to hold bearish views," one trader said.
Benchmark June platinum was up 34 yen at 1,423 yen.
"For platinum, buying, especially from Engelhard Corp was detected from the opening," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
The reports that Russia's platinum group export agency (Almaz) is to close its Tokyo office by early September also provided psychological support to the PGM market.
Gold futures also ended higher as the dollar climbed further against the yen.
The spot July gold expired at noon, up eight at 1,222 yen per gram. Benchmark June gold was up 16 yen at 1,213 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $325.25/75 per ounce at 0748 GMT, against $325.75/326.25 in New York on Friday.
"Private investors bought gold futures on the belief that the yen's weaker tendency will continue, but the upside was capped by profit-taking," one trader said.

In morning trade in Tokyo, the dollar rose as high as 1.8465 marks, its highest level since November 1989, and the dollar's strength against the mark spilled over against the yen. Benchmark June silver rose by 4.5 yen per 10 grams at 166.5 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
